newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil steady at European vegetable oil close.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil steady at European vegetable oil close.

text.p: Palm oil prices held steady at the close the European vegetable oil market on Monday.
Traders said the market had made its usual slow start to the week with business further restricted by the holiday in the U.S.
Palm oil prices held gains made after the Malaysian market closed higher as speculators played on the seasonally lower output.
Data released by Malaysian cargo surveyor SGS had little impact as it contained no surprises.
SGS put local exports at 203,609 tonnes for the first fifteen days of February against Malaysian trade estimates of 230,000 tonnes.
"The lower-than-expected SGS figures took some of the shine off the Malaysian futures towards the close, but it was only to be expected at this time of year," said one trader.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $5 down to $5 up after Mar traded at $585 and Feb traded in switch with Mar at a $% premium, but traders could give no further details.
Products closed around $2.50 up with no further business reported.
Coconut oil closed $7.50 down to unchanged after Jan/Feb traded at $785 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil finished $5 up and tradeless.
Soft oils closed unchanged to 0.50 guilders higher with most players sidelined by the holiday in the U.S.
